method: Read diff.patch (7 files, +1269/-3) against TASK.md and the surrounding prototypes/rust sources (profile.rs loader, cli.rs parse_opts, main.rs emit/plain, envelope.rs to_line/exit_code). No tests rerun; evaluation results taken as given.
ascii_fold_check: verified by reading: rule 1 host key uses str::to_ascii_lowercase; rule 5 folds via to_ascii_lowercase only when a byte is_ascii_uppercase (Cow borrow otherwise). Both map only A-Z. Unit tests also cover U+212A KELVIN SIGN, U+00DC/U+00FC, A-umlaut and sharp-s near misses.

defects.description: Wall-clock assertion (lint of 100k labels < 2 s) in a unit test; may flake on a heavily loaded host or in a debug build under contention. The complexity is evidently linear, so a count-based or ignored perf test would be more robust.

Hand-written JSON serializer duplicates the envelope shape (member order, schema_version, warnings, next) instead of going through Envelope. It is pinned by a byte-identity unit test against Envelope::to_line, so drift is caught, but any future envelope change has to be made in two places. The justification (peak RSS on a 1 MiB, 262k-label profile) is documented.

De-duplication relies on places being in non-decreasing destination order, enforced only by debug_assert. True for all five rules today, but a future rule that emits out of order would silently produce repeated ids in release builds.

correctness_notes: Input handling reuses profile::load_file and copies the profile show error branch verbatim (same stderr line, envelope, exit), so SCHEMA_INVALID/INPUT_TOO_LARGE/USAGE_ERROR/K2/K14/K15/K18 parity holds by construction; an integration test compares stdout, stderr and exit byte for byte against profile show on 11 inputs in 3 option modes.
Option parsing reuses parse_opts with the same flags as profile show: either order, missing value, unknown flag, repeated flag -> exit 2 with USAGE_ERROR JSON only with --json.

Rule 5 'two or more different spellings' is computed as any member spelling != the group's first spelling, which is equivalent. Same-destination case variants go to rule 5 only; exact duplicates go to rule 4; identical labels across destinations produce nothing.
Effective port comes from the loader default (22); port 0 is rejected by the loader, so 1..1023 except 22 is correct.
destination_ids cannot repeat ids because the loader rejects duplicate destination ids.
Closed-stdout write errors are ignored as in emit/plain, so exit parity (K12) holds; default_signals applied to ProfileLint like ProfileShow.
security_notes: No profile value in stdout/stderr: messages are fixed strings, key paths are built from fixed ASCII plus integer indexes, ids are escaped via serde_json. Plain output omits even ids. Error path is unchanged K18 loader output.
Resources bounded by the existing 1 MiB input cap; each rule is a single hash-map pass; output size is linear in labels. No file writes, no network.
test_quality_notes: 15 lint unit tests (each rule, near misses, ordering, rule 4/5 interplay, ASCII-only fold, exact four members, non-echo, byte identity with Envelope), 2 parser tests, 8 binary tests (exact JSON both orders on a path with spaces and non-ASCII, non-echo in all modes, clean fixtures, large-100 fixture, error parity with show, K14 FIFO/dir/device/socket within 2 s, usage errors, closed-stdout parity, no file writes via directory snapshot).
summary: Correct and conformant; no blocker or major defects found. ASCII-only folding confirmed by code reading. Three minor maintainability/robustness notes.
